metadata.name: lsof
metadata.displayName: lsof - List open files and processes
metadata.description: List open files and the processes using them

installation.note: lsof is commonly installed by default on many Linux distributions; if missing: sudo apt install lsof

overview.summary: lsof lists open files (regular files, directories, sockets, pipes, etc.) and the processes that have them open. It is essential for finding what process is using a file, port, or device—for example, why a disk cannot be unmounted or which process holds a port.
when_to_use: Find which process is using a file or directory (e.g., preventing umount)
See which process is listening on or using a port
List all files opened by a specific process

syntax.description: Without NAME, lsof lists all open files (often requires root). NAME can be a file path, device, or other selector.

options.description: List network files. SELECTOR can be :port, @host, etc. (e.g., -i :80 or -i TCP)
options.use_case: Find process using a specific port

options.description: List open files for the given process ID(s)
options.use_case: See everything a process has open

options.description: List only files opened by the given user(s)
List only files opened by processes whose command name matches the given pattern

examples.title: What is using a mount point
examples.description: Show processes with files open under /mnt (e.g., why umount fails)

examples.title: What is using port 80
examples.description: List processes listening on or connected to TCP port 80
examples.use_case: Find which web server holds port 80

examples.title: Files opened by a process
examples.description: List all open files for process ID 1234
examples.use_case: Debug or audit a specific process

common_pitfalls.issue: No permission to see all processes
common_pitfalls.description: Non-root users see only their own processes; many open files are hidden.
common_pitfalls.solution: Use sudo lsof when you need system-wide or another user's open files.

related_commands.description: Identify processes using a file or socket (e.g., fuser -k /mnt)
List sockets (network connections); lsof -i shows more process context
